objective_for_doctor: A 7-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a cough, sensitive pain, and burning pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. I have a really bad cough and burning, sensitive pain in my throat. Both my tonsils hurt, and my throat/thyroid cartilage area feels painful too, with some nasal congestion or a clear runny nose.

Doctor: Thanks—how long has this been going on, and do you have fever or trouble swallowing?  
Doctor: Also, is the cough dry or with mucus, and have you noticed white patches on your tonsils or swollen neck glands?  
Doctor: Lastly, any recent sick contacts, and are your symptoms worse at night or when lying down?

It started pretty fast—about a day or so (pain onset speed 5/10). I don’t know about fever, and I’m not sure about trouble swallowing. My cough is there, but I don’t know if it’s dry or with mucus, and I haven’t noticed any white patches or swollen neck glands. I’ve been around someone sick in the last couple weeks, and it feels worse when I’m lying down at night.

Doctor: Given the fast onset, throat burning, cough worse when lying down, and clear runny nose, I’m thinking more about viral pharyngitis with post-nasal drip than strep—do you have hoarseness or a runny nose that’s definitely clear?  
Doctor: Also, can you check/answer: is there any fever (≥38°C) and does coughing feel worse after meals or when you first wake up?
I don’t know about hoarseness, but my runny nose is clear. I don’t know about fever (≥38°C). And yes, it seems worse after I wake up and when I’m lying down, but I’m not sure about after meals.

Doctor: I’ll check a few things—can you tell me if you have any shortness of breath or wheezing, and whether your voice sounds “nasal/hoarse” or normal?  
Doctor: Also, I’m going to request an exam finding: do you see redness or swelling in your throat/tonsils, and do you have any tender lumps under your jaw?

I don’t know about shortness of breath or wheezing. My voice I think is a little hoarse, but I’m not totally sure. I also don’t know if my throat looks red or swollen, and I don’t know about tender lumps under my jaw.

Doctor: I’m going to request an exam finding on my side: please let me look—do you see tonsillar redness/swelling and any white exudate, and does your neck have tender lymph nodes under the jaw or along the sides?  
Doctor: Also, REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test (or throat swab) so we can rule out strep quickly in a 7-year-old.

I don’t know what my throat looks like from the outside, and I can’t check for white exudate or redness myself. I also don’t know if I have tender lymph nodes under my jaw or along the sides. You can do the throat swab/test.

Doctor: Thanks—I'll proceed with the throat swab; while that’s running, do you have fever/chills now, and has the cough included any barking sound or fast breathing?  
Doctor: Also, is the pain mainly worse when you swallow liquids, and do you have any belly pain, vomiting, or rash?

I don’t know about fever or chills right now. I also don’t know if the cough is barking or if my breathing is fast. My throat pain is worse when I swallow liquids, but I don’t have belly pain, vomiting, or a rash.

Doctor: Thanks—given the 1-day rapid onset, clear runny nose, hoarse voice, cough worse lying down/at night, and throat pain worse with swallowing liquids, this still sounds most like a viral upper-respiratory infection with post-nasal drip rather than strep; can you tell me if she has any trouble breathing or “stridor” (noisy breathing when resting)?  
Doctor: If her rapid strep result comes back negative, I’ll treat supportively; REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test result (and culture if available).
I don’t know if she has trouble breathing or any noisy breathing at rest. The main thing is the throat burning/sensitive pain and the cough that feels worse at night and when lying down.

Doctor: I’m going to do a quick focused exam now—can you tell me whether she has any swollen “sandpaper” rash, and I’ll assess vitals (temp, pulse, oxygen) and throat/tonsils for erythema/exudate and tender cervical nodes.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test result (and throat culture if rapid is negative).
I don’t have any rash like that. I don’t know the vitals or what the exam shows in her throat/tonsils, but you can check and do the rapid strep test (and culture if it’s negative).

Doctor: I’m getting the Rapid Strep result and I’ll also check her throat directly for erythema/exudate plus tender cervical nodes. Does she have any breathing difficulty or noisy breathing at rest?  
Doctor: If Rapid Strep is negative and she’s otherwise stable, this fits best with viral pharyngitis/post-nasal drip (laryngopharyngeal reflux-like irritation can also cause burning) rather than strep—what did her Rapid Strep show?  
DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral pharyngitis / viral URI with post-nasal drip (strep less likely pending negative Rapid Strep).

[DDX]
1. Viral pharyngitis
